entries.s: Fever in the elderly may only have "weird" symptoms: poor appetite, lethargy, confusion, and falls. Notification is required if the body temperature is ≥38℃ or more than 1℃ higher than usual.
entries.why: The elderly have a weak immune response and may not have an obvious fever during pneumonia or urinary tract infection. Changes in consciousness or behavior may occur first.
steps: Take the temperature and record it; at the same time, check the respiratory rate, blood oxygen, and pulse.
Look for possible sources: cough with phlegm (lungs), cloudy urine and frequent urination (urinary system), red and swollen wounds (skin), diarrhea and vomiting (stomach).
Replenish moisture, reduce clothing, and wipe with warm water; do not cover it up to "force sweat".
The following → 119: Body temperature ≥39°C combined with changes in consciousness, shortness of breath, blood oxygen <92%, decreased blood pressure, and purple spots on the skin.
The rest of the report is to the supervisor and it is recommended that the family members seek medical treatment; antipyretic drugs should be taken according to the doctor's instructions.
Record time, temperature, symptoms and treatment.
no: Do not self-administer fever reducers or antibiotics.
Do not use alcohol to rub your body.
Don't ignore sudden confusion or lethargy just because "you don't have a fever."
entries.rep: Fever combined with changes in consciousness, difficulty breathing, and low blood pressure → 119; Generally, notify the supervisor of fever and recommend medical treatment.
entries.ref: Principles for identifying signs of infection in the elderly; delirium screening.
entries.ask: The patient has suddenly become very confused in the past two days but his body temperature is normal. In addition to fever, what other signs of infection can be seen?

entries.t: Altered consciousness or inability to wake
entries.s: Unable to wake up or sudden worsening of reaction: confirm breathing → lie on side → 119. It’s 119 even if you’re breathing but can’t wake up.
entries.why: There are many reasons for altered consciousness (stroke, hypoglycemia, drugs, infection, cerebral hemorrhage). You don't need to judge the cause, you only need to judge "whether to call 119".
steps: Tap your shoulder and call your name loudly to see if there is any response.
No response: Check the chest for 10 seconds to see if there is breathing; no breathing or only wheezing → Call 119. Start CPR (chest compressions 100–120 times per minute, depth 5 cm).
Breathing → Lie on your side (resuscitation position) to prevent choking, call 119.
Measure blood sugar when a blood glucose machine is available; have diabetes and <70 → do not feed, wait for rescue.
Prepare the medication list, health insurance card, and ID card, and inform the supervisor and family members.
Record the time of discovery, status at that time, and what you did.
no: Do not shake your head and neck.
Do not feed water or medicine.
Don't be unsure just because "he often sleeps for a long time".
entries.rep: Direct 119; then notify the supervisor and family members.
entries.ref: Basic Life-Saving (BLS) Procedures; EMS Act Section 14-2.
entries.ask: The client has a DNR (do not perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation) and I find that he is not breathing. What should I do?

entries.t: Dislodged nasogastric tube or urinary catheter
entries.s: Do not reinsert it yourself. If the nasogastric tube is dislodged, stop tube feeding and record its exposed length. If the urinary catheter is dislodged, check for bleeding, report and arrange replacement by appropriate staff.
entries.why: Home care workers must not insert these tubes. Incorrect insertion can send feed into the lungs or injure the urethra.
steps: If the nasogastric tube comes out completely, stop tube feeding and medication administration through it. Keep the tube for the nurse to inspect and record the time and the person's condition, including any coughing or choking.
If the nasogastric tube has partly slipped out (its external marking has changed), do not push it back and do not feed through it. Secure it and report.

The urinary catheter falls off: Check whether there is bleeding from the urethra orifice, encourage drinking water, and record whether there is voluntary urination; 8 hours without urination or lower abdominal distension → seek medical advice.
Notify the supervisor and contact home care for relocation or medical treatment according to unit procedures.
Find out the cause of detachment (self-extraction of the client, loosening of fixation, shifting and pulling), and discuss prevention with the supervisor.
no: Do not plug the tube back in yourself.
Do not continue tube feeding after the tube is dislodged.
Do not blame the client for extricating himself.
entries.rep: Notify supervision if all tubes fall off; combined with bleeding, shortness of breath, severe abdominal distension → 119.
entries.ref: Taiwan Nursing Personnel Act: tube insertion is a nursing or medical procedure; the provider’s procedure for tube-related incidents.
entries.ask: The client has been self-extracting the nasogastric tube. Are there any practices that can reduce self-extraction without restraint?

entries.s: If you find that you missed taking medicine, took it repeatedly, or took medicine from the wrong person: do not "make up for it" or "induced vomiting", report it immediately and observe the symptoms.
entries.why: The first reaction when dealing with an error is often to remedy the problem on your own, but taking supplementary food may lead to overdose, and vomiting may result in choking.
steps: Confirm: what to eat, how many pills, what time, what should be eaten.
Immediately notify the supervisor, and the unit will contact the pharmacist, home care or physician to determine whether treatment is needed.
Observe the patient: dizziness, drowsiness, abnormal heartbeat, changes in blood pressure and blood sugar, and breathing.
Changes in consciousness, difficulty breathing, and convulsions → 119, and inform what medicine was taken.
Record events and observations and keep medicine bag.
Review the medication distribution method with the supervisor and family members afterwards.
no: Do not take more or less medicine by yourself.
Do not induce vomiting.
Do not hide or hide medicine.
entries.rep: Report all medication errors to supervisor; symptomatic → 119 or poison consultation.
entries.ref: Standards for notification of abnormal drug use in units; Pharmaceutical Affairs Law.
entries.ask: The client took two blood pressure lowering drugs in the morning and is not feeling uncomfortable at the moment. What should I observe in the next few hours?

entries.s: First understand the reasons (physical discomfort, mood, distrust of people), you can change the method and time, do not force; record and report.
entries.why: Forcing will damage the relationship and the client's rights; but not dealing with it at all will cause the client's basic needs to be ignored.
steps: First confirm whether there are any physical reasons: pain, discomfort, sleepiness, and need to go to the toilet.
Invite again in the way he is familiar with: change the words, change the order, do what he likes first.
Still refuse: respect, but confirm basic safety (water, food, environment is safe), and do other projects that can be done.
Record the rejected projects, your invitation method, and what the client said.
Notify the supervisor and discuss whether it is necessary to adjust service content, time or personnel.
If the application is rejected multiple times in a row, the supervisor will discuss it with the family members and personal manager.
no: Don't use threats ("I'll repay you if you don't shower").
Do not do it secretly or while the client is sleeping.
Do not write down the rejection as “the client does not cooperate” without writing down the reasons.
entries.rep: Continuous refusal affects basic care (not eating, not drinking, not cleaning for more than one day) → notify the supervisor; suspected refusal due to illness → suggest medical treatment.
entries.ref: Service user autonomy under the Long-term Care Services Act; Unit Service Standards.
entries.ask: The client refuses me to help him bathe every time, but accepts another waiter. How can I adjust?

entries.s: Keep distance from exits, reduce stimulation, and do not argue; if there is immediate danger, leave the scene and call the supervisor or 110.
entries.why: Your safety comes first. Most aggression comes from fear, pain, or misunderstanding, and reducing the stimulus is usually more effective than suppressing it.
steps: Stand to the side of the client, at least an arm's length away, so that you are on the side closest to the door.
Slow down your tone and say a short sentence: "I know you are angry, let me step away first."
Turn off the TV, ask others to leave, and reduce stimulation.
Do not snatch or suppress; leave the room if he has dangerous objects in his hands.
Return after the person has calmed down. Do not confront them about the earlier incident.
If you are injured or in immediate danger → leave the scene and call 110, and notify the supervisor; handle and record the incident according to the illegal infringement process.
no: Do not turn your back to the client or box yourself into a corner.
Do not attempt to subdue alone.
Don’t bear it alone afterwards. This is an illegal violation in the workplace, and the unit is responsible for handling it.
entries.rep: All aggressive behaviors are reported to the supervisor and recorded; injuries → seek medical treatment and leave a medical certificate, and handle according to occupational accident and illegal infringement procedures.
entries.ref: Article 6, Item 2 of the Occupational Safety and Health Law (Prevention of illegal physical or mental harm due to the behavior of others while performing duties); Principles for handling dementia behavior.
entries.ask: The client is mentally ill and has a record of assault. Please help me list 5 safety preparations that can be made before entering the door.

entries.t: No answer at the door or loss of contact
entries.s: Calling, knocking on doors, asking neighbors, contacting emergency contacts and supervisors; living alone and acting strangely (lights on, smells, sounds) → 110/119.
entries.why: It is one of the most regrettable events for an elderly person living alone to collapse at home and not be found. You may be the only one who will find out.
steps: Knock on the door, ring the bell, and call the client 2–3 times, a few minutes apart.
Observe: whether the lights are on, whether the shoes are there, whether there is any peculiar smell, whether there is any call for help or the sound of TV.
Call the emergency contact person/family member to confirm whether you are going out or hospitalized.
Contact the supervisor, and the unit will decide whether to ask family members to open the door or ask the police for assistance.
There are obvious abnormalities (hearing groans, smelling gas or rotten smell) → Directly 110/119.
Record arrival time, method and results of contact attempts.
no: Do not break down doors or climb through windows yourself.
Don't just leave a note and leave without informing yourself.
entries.rep: Report all lost contacts to the supervisor; if there is any abnormality, please call 110/119.
entries.ref: Unit service exception handling specifications; long-term care benefits and payment standards BA22 related to safe viewing.
entries.ask: No one answered the door for 20 minutes after I arrived at the case’s home, and the family members did not answer their calls. Please help me list the next things to do and the order.

entries.t: Gas odor, fire and electric shock
entries.s: Gas: Do not turn on electrical appliances, open windows, turn off the main switch, take the client away and then call 119. Fire: Take people away first, close the door, and go to a safe place before reporting the incident.
entries.why: Home fires and gas leaks often occur in families with elderly people. Your action (turning on the light) may cause an explosion.
steps: Gas smell: Do not turn on or off any electrical appliances (including lights and exhaust fans), do not use lighters; gently open the window, turn off the gas main switch, and take the client outside the house to turn on 119 the gas company.
Low heat (pot fire): Turn off the fire source, cover the pot, and do not splash water.
The fire is uncontrollable: take the client away, close the door when leaving (to slow down the fire), do not take the elevator, go to a safe place and call 119.
People with reduced mobility: wrap them in quilts and drag them or carry them in wheelchairs or chairs; lower your body when there is heavy smoke.
Electric shock: Cut off the power supply (main switch) first and then touch the client. If it cannot be cut off, use a dry wooden stick to push it away; no breathing → CPR, 119.
Notify supervisor and family members, record.
no: Do not return to a fire to salvage property.
Do not turn on the lights or make phone calls when there is a smell of gas (go outside the house before making calls).
Do not pull the electrocuted person directly with your hands.
entries.rep: Direct 119; notify the supervisor afterwards.
entries.ref: Fire Department Home Fire Prevention and Escape Guidelines.
entries.ask: The client often forgets to turn off the gas stove. In addition to warnings, what other safety devices or practices can the family members be advised?

entries.s: If you see injuries, have been unclean for a long time, been locked up, been insulted, or had property misappropriated: do not ask questions or confront, record the facts, and report within 24 hours.
entries.why: Housekeepers are legally responsible for notifying people. Failure to report something they see is not only a moral issue, but also a legal responsibility.
steps: Observe and record the facts: the location and shape of the injury (fingerprints, strangulation marks, burn marks), time, the client’s statement (in quotation marks for the original text), and environmental conditions (presence of food, cleaning, medicine).
Do not confront the family members, do not blame them, and do not promise "I will not tell anyone."
Confirm that the client is safe at the moment; there is immediate danger → 110.
Immediately notify the supervisor, and the unit will notify 113 or the local competent authority within 24 hours according to regulations; you can also call 113 directly.
Protect the privacy of the client and yourself and do not discuss in the group.
Subsequently, follow the instructions of the unit and social workers.
no: Do not take photos of the client’s injuries and upload them to the group (it can be handled by the supervisor according to the unit’s instructions).
Don’t refuse to report just because “the family members are generally nice people”.
Do not confront or try to punish the family yourself.
entries.rep: Report to supervision +113 (protection hotline), and complete statutory notification within 24 hours.
entries.ref: Article 43 of the Elderly Welfare Law (responsibility notification, within 24 hours at the latest); Article 76 of the Law on the Protection of Rights and Interests of Persons with Disabilities; Article 50 of the Domestic Violence Prevention Law.
entries.ask: I saw bruises on the client’s arm that looked like finger grips. The family members said they were hit by themselves. Please help me write an objective observation record.

entries.t: Finding a client who may have died
entries.s: Confirm that there is no breathing and pulse: if there is no DNR, then CPR+119; if there is DNR or obvious signs of death, do not move or clean up the scene, and notify 119/110 and supervisor.
entries.why: Resident staff cannot declare death; the way the person is handled at the scene will affect subsequent legal procedures, and they must also take care of their own mood.
steps: Unable to wake up, no breathing, no pulse: If there are no obvious signs of death (rigor mortis, mortem spots, cold body) and no DNR → call 119 and perform CPR.
If there is DNR (relaxation wish) or obvious signs of death → do not rescue, do not move the body, do not clean up the scene, and do not extubate.
Call 119 (confirmed by ambulance or doctor). If the death is unnatural or the circumstances are unknown, the police will arrive at the scene and provide explanations.
Notify the supervisor and family members immediately; do not stay alone for too long and ask the supervisor or family members to be present.
Record the time of discovery, status at that time, what you did, and who you reported to.
Talk to the supervisor afterwards and the unit should provide psychological support.
no: Do not move remains or clean up the environment.
Do not notify the undertaker yourself.
Do not discuss the cause of the client’s death with others.
entries.rep: 119/110+supervision+family members.
entries.ref: Hospice and Palliative Care Regulations (DNR); Criminal Procedure Code Unnatural Death Reporting Procedures.
entries.ask: It was the first time I encountered the death of a client, and I was very sad afterwards. What methods can I use to help myself? What support should the unit provide?

entries.t: Worker injuries: back strain, bites, needlesticks and falls
entries.s: Treat the wound first, seek medical attention and leave a medical certificate, and report the accident on the same day. This is an occupational accident, and there will be public injury leave and benefits.
entries.why: Many home care workers do not report their injuries and use pain-relief patches themselves. Their injuries may become chronic, and they may miss out on protection and benefits.
steps: Make sure the client is safe first (if you are unable to continue serving, notify the supervisor to arrange for a replacement).
Wound treatment: Bleeding compression, needle pricking, squeezing blood immediately and flushing with water, animal bites flushing for 15 minutes.
Seek medical treatment that day, told the doctor that he was "injured at work" and obtained a diagnosis.
Notify the supervisor on the same day and fill out an occupational disaster report; blood will be drawn to track the acupuncture.
Keep medical records, receipts, service records of the day and relevant evidence.
Apply for benefits in accordance with the Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act and take public sick leave (without salary deduction).
no: Don’t “just rest for a few days” without recording.
Do not take painkillers yourself and continue working.
Do not fail to report an injury because you are afraid of inconveniencing your employer.
entries.rep: Notify supervision and occupational accident notification; consult the Labor Bureau or 1955 when necessary.
entries.ref: Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act; Labor Leave Rules Article 6 (Public Sickness Leave); Occupational Safety and Health Act.
entries.ask: When I was moving the client, I slipped up to my waist. I have already seen a doctor. Please tell me what documents and procedures I need to prepare to apply for occupational disaster benefits.

entries.s: The client has unknown itching all over the body, which is more itchy at night, and rash on the finger joints → suspected scabies; wear gloves and isolation gown, notify and arrange for medical treatment, and treat the clothes with hot water.
entries.why: Scabies spreads quickly in homes and institutions, and the attendants themselves are part of the chain of transmission.
steps: Protection: Disposable gloves, isolation gown or overalls, wash hands and change clothes after service.
Suspected scabies: Notify the supervisor, and it is recommended to seek medical treatment for diagnosis; the client and those who live with him should be treated at the same time.
Wash clothes and bed sheets in hot water above 60℃ or seal in plastic bags for more than 7 days.
You should also seek medical attention if you experience itching or rash. This is an occupational disease.
Other infectious diseases (influenza, gastroenteritis, COVID): Wear a mask, wash hands frequently, and adjust services according to unit regulations if you have symptoms.
no: Do not handle client’s clothing and bed linen without protection.
Do not hide symptoms and continue serving.
entries.rep: Notify supervision; follow unit infection control regulations.
entries.ref: Department of Disease Control and Prevention Scabies Prevention and Treatment Guidelines; Institutional Infection Control Code.
entries.ask: Someone in the family has been diagnosed with scabies. What cleaning and follow-up should I do after today’s service?

entries.t: Understanding workplace violence and unlawful abuse
entries.s: Verbal abuse, intimidation, physical violence, and sexual harassment by the client or family members are all illegal violations in the workplace; employers have statutory obligations to prevent and deal with them.
entries.why: Many home care workers think being verbally abused by a client is part of the job. The law does not regard it that way.
steps: Four types: physical violence (hitting, pushing, throwing things), psychological violence (abuse, intimidation, humiliation), verbal violence, and sexual harassment.
At the moment of the incident: ensure safety, leave the scene, and notify the supervisor (telephone).
Record that day: time, location, words and deeds of the other party (original text), your reaction, whether there are witnesses, and whether there is a recording.
Units are required by law to: accept, investigate, provide assistance (medical, psychological, legal), replace waiters or terminate services when necessary, and prevent recurrence.
You can ask the unit to provide the processing results; if the unit does not handle the matter, you can appeal to the Labor Bureau.
It is an occupational accident to seek medical treatment for an injury and leave a medical certificate.
no: Don’t think “just tolerate it” and not record it.
Do not confront the person alone.
Do not settle privately or accept money to settle matters.
entries.rep: Notify the supervisor + written record; the unit did not handle → appeal to the local labor bureau or 1955.
entries.ref: Article 6, Paragraph 2, Paragraph 3, of the Occupational Safety and Health Act; Article 324-3 of the Occupational Safety and Health Facilities Regulations (the employer shall formulate a plan to prevent unlawful infringement in the performance of duties); Ministry of Labor’s Guidelines on the Prevention of Unlawful Infringement in the Performing of Duties.
entries.ask: Please help me organize this experience into an illegal infringement report record, and list the handling items that I can propose to the unit: (Describe the incident).

entries.t: Sexual harassment by a client or family member
entries.s: Sexual harassment is not your fault. Clearly refuse, leave, and notify the unit on the same day; the unit must accept the investigation and protect you in accordance with the Gender Equality Work Law.
entries.why: Housekeepers work in private residences and have a lot of physical contact, making them an occupation with a high risk of sexual harassment; after the law is revised in 2024, the employer's responsibilities will be clearer.
steps: Now: Say clearly "please stop, this is sexual harassment", leave the scene, and do not need to continue serving.
On the same day: Notify the supervisor by phone and record in writing (time, location, original words and deeds, body contact parts, witnesses).
File a complaint with the unit; the unit should immediately take effective corrective and remedial measures (adjust services, change clients, assist with medical treatment or psychological support).

You can complain to the local labor bureau at the same time (the employer has not handled it), or you can complain to the county or city authorities in accordance with the Sexual Harassment Prevention and Control Act, or report the case to the police.

Limitation of appeal: The Sexual Equality Law stipulates that within 2 years from the date of becoming aware of the incident and within 5 years from the occurrence of the incident; it is recommended to do so as soon as possible.
Severe cases (forced touching) may result in criminal prosecution (Article 25 of the Sexual Harassment Prevention and Control Act).
no: Do not dismiss the incident because the person has dementia or is older. Report it so the provider can assess how to respond.
Do not delete messages, photos, and other evidence.
Don’t go back to the same client alone.
entries.rep: Report to supervisor + appeal; Labor Bureau/1955/113/110.
entries.ref: Articles 12 and 13 of the Gender Equality at Work Law (Employer’s Obligations to Prevent and Control and Treatment upon Knowledge); Sexual Harassment Prevention and Control Law; Article 6, Item 2 of the Occupational Safety and Health Law.
entries.ask: The client’s family members said sexually suggestive words to me many times. I have told the supervisor but nothing happened. What else can I do?

entries.s: First, obtain a medical examination and obtain a diagnosis certificate, report to the police, and notify the unit; the crime of injury is subject to complaint and must be filed within 6 months.
entries.why: The most important things after an injury are "evidence" and "time". If you miss it, you cannot pursue it.
steps: Leave the scene to ensure safety and call 110 (in immediate danger).
Seek medical examination for injuries that day, explain to the doctor that he was injured by someone else, and obtain a diagnosis.
Report the crime to the police (it does not have to be filed immediately, but it must be recorded).
Notify the supervisor and fill in the illegal infringement and occupational disaster report.
Preserve evidence: photos of injuries, conversation records, eyewitness contact information.

Whether to file a complaint shall be discussed with the employer and the legal support; for the crime of injury (Article 277 of the Criminal Law), the complaint is non-committal and must be filed within 6 months after becoming aware of the crime.
no: Don’t fight back (it will turn into a fight).
Do not withdraw the notification upon accepting a verbal apology.
entries.rep: 110 + seek medical treatment + report to supervision; for legal consultation, please contact the Legal Aid Foundation or the Labor Bureau.
entries.ref: Penal Code Article 277 Crime of Injury; Criminal Procedure Law Article 237 Complaint Period 6 Months; Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Law.
entries.ask: The family member of the case pushed me and hit the corner of the table, causing bruises. Do I want to file a lawsuit? Please list the consequences of filing a complaint or not filing a complaint.

entries.t: Mandatory reporting of elder abuse and neglect
entries.s: Residential staff are responsible for reporting: if they learn that an elderly person is suspected of abuse, neglect, abandonment, or misappropriation of property, they must report it within 24 hours at the latest.
entries.why: Responsibility notification is a legal obligation, and failure to notify may result in fines; after notification, it will be handled by the competent authority, and you do not need to investigate by yourself.
steps: Circumstances to be reported: physical abuse, emotional abuse, neglect (denial of food, medicine, cleaning), abandonment, misappropriation of property, leaving in dangerous environment.
After discovery, record the facts and notify the supervisor immediately, and the unit will report to the local competent authority (you can also directly dial 113), within 24 hours at the latest.
Contents of the report: Basic information about the case, facts you observed, time, possible perpetrators (only observations, no conclusions).
The informant’s information is protected by confidentiality.
Cooperate with social workers for follow-up visits.
no: Don’t wait for “confirmation of abuse” before reporting. The law requires reporting “suspected” abuse.
Do not fail to report for fear of family retaliation. The identity of the reporter will be kept confidential.
entries.rep: Supervision +113 (within 24 hours).
entries.ref: Article 43 of the Elderly Welfare Law (Responsibility notification of doctors, social workers, village chiefs, police, and other personnel involved in the implementation of elderly welfare services; failure to notify shall result in a fine of not less than NT$6,000 but not more than NT$30,000); Articles 41 and 51.
entries.ask: There is no food in the refrigerator at the client’s home, the medicine is expired, and the family only comes once a week. Is this considered negligence? How do I report this?

entries.t: Reporting abuse of people with disabilities and domestic violence
entries.s: Abuse of persons with disabilities must also be reported within 24 hours; violence between family members living together is domestic violence and is also a duty to report.
entries.why: The client may not necessarily be an elderly person, but may also be a physically or mentally disabled person; if the perpetrator is a family member, it also involves domestic violence prevention and treatment.
steps: Persons with disabilities: Suspected abandonment, abuse, physical and mental abuse, property misappropriation, leaving in dangerous environment → report within 24 hours.
Domestic violence: physical, mental, financial abuse between family members → Notification 113, the victim may apply for a protection order.
Record the facts, notify the supervisor, or dial 113 directly by the unit or you.
The client is in immediate danger → 110.
Cooperate with social workers and competent authorities after reporting.
no: Do not attempt to mediate family disputes.
Do not discuss reporting matters in front of the offender.
entries.rep: Supervision +113; Immediate Danger 110.
entries.ref: Article 76 of the Law on the Protection of Rights and Interests of Persons with Disabilities (24-hour notification of responsibilities), Article 75 (Prohibited Behavior); Article 50 of the Domestic Violence Prevention Law.
entries.ask: The client is a 50-year-old mentally and physically disabled person. His brother often yells insults at him and withholds his subsidy. What is the scope of notification?

entries.s: The patient’s condition, address, family situation, and photos are all personal information: no photos will be uploaded, no group discussions will be held, and no public disclosure will be made.
entries.why: Posting a photo of a client to a group to "ask colleagues for advice" is the most common illegal situation and may involve criminal liability and civil compensation.
steps: Service records are only written in the unit system or designated forms, and do not exist on personal mobile phones.
When it is necessary to take pictures (wounds, environment), the supervisor shall instruct in accordance with unit regulations, and no face pictures or uploading to private groups will be allowed.
The client information will not be disclosed to unauthorized persons, including neighbors, other clients, and family members.
No case client information will be retained after resignation or case closure.
The client or family members will not answer any questions about the status of other clients.
If a colleague violates the rules, report it to the supervisor.
no: Do not post photos or videos of the victim on social media, even if he does not show his face.
Do not use private LINE to send a copy of the patient’s medical records or ID card.
Do not give information to unauthorized persons just because it is “for the client’s benefit”.
entries.rep: If personal information is discovered to be leaked, report it to the supervisor and the unit will handle it in accordance with personal information laws.
entries.ref: Articles 5, 20, and 41 of the Personal Data Protection Law (illegal use of personal information shall be punishable by criminal liability); confidentiality obligations under the Long-term Care Services Law; unit information security regulations.
entries.ask: The family asked me to send him photos of the client during daily service. Is there any problem with this? How can I respond?

entries.t: Legal limits on recording for self-protection
entries.s: The conversations you participate in can be recorded for self-protection; however, you are not allowed to secretly photograph the client’s body or private space, and they are not allowed to be made public or distributed.
entries.why: Recording is the most effective evidence when someone is abused or sexually harassed, but if done in the wrong way, you may break the law.
steps: Principle: A conversation in which you personally participate is recorded in order to protect your own rights. In practice, it is generally considered that it does not constitute an obstruction of secrets.
The recording content is only provided to work units, police, and courts, and is not posted online or distributed to groups.
It is not allowed to film the client’s private activities such as changing clothes, using the toilet, or bathing, even if it is to “prove that I did it.”

There is a monitor in the case’s home: the family members have the right to install it in their home, but if the bathroom is filmed or used to humiliate or spread, it can reflect the work unit’s handling.
The recorded content should be kept properly and the supervisor should be informed of the recording when reporting.
no: Do not leave the recording device behind the suspect’s home (conversations in which you are not involved are secretly recorded).
Do not threaten the other party with recordings.
Do not edit or provide only snippets.
entries.rep: The recording evidence shall be handed over to the supervisor and the unit for preservation; in case of litigation, lawyers or legal aid shall assist.
entries.ref: Penal Code Article 315-1 (Unprovoked recording of other people’s non-public activities, speeches, conversations or private parts of the body); Communications Security and Supervision Law Article 29 Paragraph 3; Personal Data Protection Law.
entries.ask: I want to use mobile phone recording to protect myself every time I receive services. Do I need to inform the client first? Are there any situations that cannot be recorded?

entries.t: Medical procedures home care workers must not perform
entries.s: Injections, tube changes, blood draws, dressing changes (deep wounds), determining the dosage of medicine, deep sputum extraction in the trachea, etc. are medical or nursing activities and cannot be done, even if the family members ask.
entries.why: If you do medical treatment that you shouldn’t do, you will be criminally liable (a secret medical crime) when something goes wrong, and your employer’s insurance will not cover it.
steps: Can do (and requires training): Assist with eating and nasogastric tube feeding, suction of oral secretions, turn over and pat back, move limbs and joints, measure vital signs, assist in taking medication (reminder and confirmation).

Cannot do: Injections (including insulin), changing nasogastric tubes or urinary catheters, drawing blood, wound debridement and suturing, determining or adjusting drug doses, deep endotracheal tube suction (unless BA17 training is completed and approved), enemas.
When requested by family members: clearly state that "this project must be carried out by nurses according to regulations. I can help contact home care" and report it to the supervisor.
If you are unsure, ask the supervisor and don’t agree on the spot.
Document the family’s request and your response.
no: Do not give an insulin injection just because the family usually gives it themselves.
Do not perform unfamiliar operations under the guidance of family members.
entries.rep: Continued requests from family members → Notify the supervisor, and the unit will explain and refer to home care.
entries.ref: Article 28 of the Physician Act (Penalty for non-physicians performing medical services); Article 24 of the Nursing Care Act; long-term care benefits and the items that nursing staff can perform listed in the payment standards.
entries.ask: The family members want me to help the patient administer insulin, saying that this is what they do. How can I refuse without hurting the relationship?

entries.s: Only do the projects approved for the client; helping family members clean, take care of children, and take care of other elders are beyond the scope, so I declined and reported back.
entries.why: Exceeding the approved scope not only prevents declarations, but also provides no protection in case of accidents, and also excludes the services that clients really need.
steps: Check the approved items and hours clearly before service.
Housework assistance is limited to the space and items used by the client (client’s room, client’s tableware).
Encountered a request: "This project is not within the approved scope and it is not convenient for me to do it. If necessary, I can ask for supervision and evaluation."
Report to the supervisor on the same day and record the required content.
If the client has other needs, the supervisor will discuss the adjustment plan with the individual supervisor.
no: Don’t “help once in a while” – once it becomes the norm.
Do not accept additional fees for private services (violates unit rules and loses coverage).
entries.rep: Report supervision processing.
entries.ref: Long-term care service application and payment items of payment method; unit service contract.
entries.ask: Every time my family asks me to cook dinner for the whole family, please give me three different ways of saying no.

entries.s: No gift money will be accepted, no passbooks, stamped ATM cards, or loans will be taken into custody; receipts will be kept for all purchases, delivered in person, and recorded.
entries.why: Financial disputes are the most common reason for home workers to be accused; once accused, it is almost impossible to prove themselves without records.
steps: Gifts: Small amounts of food can be accepted and returned in accordance with unit regulations; cash, red envelopes, and valuables are all declined.
Purchasing agent (when approving the project): Get the money first, deliver the change and receipt in person after purchase, and record the items and amount.
The client’s bankbook, seal, ATM card, and password will not be kept in custody, even if requested by family members.
Do not lend money to or from the client.
The client took the initiative to give money and "leave you something", and reported it to the supervisor on the same day and recorded it.
no: Do not use your own money to advance and then request payment (it is easy to dispute).
Do not help the client receive money, transfer funds, or operate online banking.
Do not accept anything of value from the client to “keep for me.”
entries.rep: The client or family members take the initiative to give money → report to the supervisor; if accused of embezzlement → report immediately and keep all receipt records.
entries.ref: Criminal Law Article 335: Crime of embezzlement, Article 339: Crime of Fraud; Unit Integrity and Acceptance of Gifts.
entries.ask: The client insists on giving me red envelopes every time. I have refused many times. Please help me think of a gentle but firm response.

entries.t: Witnessing wills, property and insurance beneficiaries
entries.s: Do not serve as a witness to the will, do not intervene in the distribution of property, and do not become a beneficiary; report to the supervisor when requested.
entries.why: The resident worker has a trusting relationship with the client, and once the property is involved, it is easy for the family members to challenge the undue influence, and even the will will be invalid.
steps: The client mentioned that he wants to make a will and give you property or insurance → explain "I can't get involved in these things" and report to the supervisor on the same day.
Do not sign any documents related to property, IOUs, or contracts (including being a witness).
No one takes a stand or communicates on property disputes between family members.
When the client needs legal assistance, it is recommended that family members or social workers contact legal aid or lawyers.
no: Do not sign just because the client insists.
Do not keep wills or important documents for the client.
entries.rep: Report supervision processing.
entries.ref: Article 1198 of the Civil Code (the legatee, his spouse, and direct blood relatives shall not be witnesses of the will); Unit Ethics Code.
entries.ask: The client said he would leave the house to me because his family ignored him. How should I respond so as not to hurt his heart?

entries.t: My responsibility when a client is injured during care
entries.s: If standard operations are carried out, recorded, and reported, it will not constitute negligence; only failure to operate in accordance with regulations or concealment will lead to liability.
entries.why: Fear of being accused is the biggest source of stress for home workers, but what the law looks at is “whether the regulations were followed,” not “whether something happened.”
steps: Judgment of negligence liability: Did you pay attention to what a qualified resident attendant should do (according to training and SOP).
Three things to protect yourself: operate according to SOP, keep records of each service, and report abnormalities immediately.
When an injury occurs: deal with the client first, then report, and record the facts (do not write "my fault" or "not my fault").
The company usually has public accident liability insurance. Compensation and negotiation are handled by the company. You should not make any private commitments.
If a family member files a lawsuit, immediately notify the employer and request legal assistance (legal aid, legal counsel of the employer).
In criminal law, negligent injury is subject to prosecution, while in civil law, compensation for medical expenses, etc. may be claimed.
no: Do not apologize to family members in private to admit your fault or promise compensation.
Do not modify or overwrite records.
Do not consult with the family alone.
entries.rep: Notify the supervisor; notify the unit and seek legal support when being sued.
entries.ref: Criminal Law Article 284 Negligent Injury (not subject to complaint); Civil Law Articles 184 and 188 Torts and Employer Liability; Unit Liability Insurance.
entries.ask: The client fell to the ground while I was assisting him in the relocation. His family members said they wanted to sue me. What should I do and what should I not do now?

entries.s: When non-rescue personnel perform first aid (CPR, Hemlich, and hemostasis) to save people, the law has emergency evacuation exemption provisions, so there is no need to worry about being the wrong defendant.
entries.why: Many people are afraid of CPR for fear of the defendant breaking their ribs, but the law encourages you to save people.
steps: The Emergency Medical Rescue Law stipulates that when persons other than rescue personnel perform first-aid measures to avoid imminent danger to the lives of others, the emergency evacuation exemption under civil law and criminal law shall apply.
When giving first aid, follow your training and call 119.
Supervise and record the process of reporting after first aid.
For a client with a DNR: respect their wish not to receive CPR, but still call 119 for confirmation and report the situation.
no: Don’t hesitate to rescue because you are afraid of responsibility.
Do not do more than you are capable of (e.g. self-administer medications).
entries.rep: 119+Supervision.
entries.ref: Emergency Medical Assistance Law Article 14-2; Civil Code Article 150, Criminal Law Article 24 Emergency Evacuation.
entries.ask: I heard the client’s ribs break while doing CPR. Will I be legally responsible for this?

entries.t: Accusations of theft or property damage
entries.s: Stay calm, do not reconcile privately, and report to the unit immediately; keep the record of the day, and have the unit accompany you to call the police for clarification if necessary.
entries.why: Dementia patients often refer to "can't find" as "stolen", and family members may also misunderstand it; the way you deal with it determines whether you will be dragged into legal proceedings.
steps: Remain calm on the spot, do not argue, and say "I understand you are worried, please let the unit handle it".
Do not promise compensation or give money privately.
Immediately notify the supervisor, and the unit will intervene and communicate.
Provide your service record for the day, arrival and departure times, and whether anyone else is present.

If the other party calls the police and cooperates with the explanation, you can ask your employer to accompany you; if the accusation is false and continues to be spread, you can consult legal support (defamation, false accusation).
Daily precautions: do not enter the valuables area, do not open drawers, and keep the case owner or family members themselves.
no: Don’t rummage around to prove your innocence.
Do not sign any documents of acknowledgment or compensation.
entries.rep: Notify and supervise handling; police and legal support when necessary.
entries.ref: Criminal Law Article 320 Crime of Theft, Article 169 Crime of False Accusation, Article 310 Crime of Defamation; unit complaint and handling process.
entries.ask: A client’s family says NT$3000 is missing from a wallet and implies that I took it. How should I respond and follow up?

entries.s: Injuries at work or on the way to and from the client’s home, and illnesses acquired due to work (back injuries, scabies) are all occupational disasters, and are entitled to public sick leave and insurance benefits.
entries.why: Resident workers are an occupation with a high risk of occupational accidents, but the notification rate is extremely low; only by knowing your rights can you protect yourself.
steps: Scope: injuries during service, traffic accidents between two clients’ homes or reasonable routes to and from work, and illnesses caused by work.
Seek medical treatment that day and informed the doctor that the injury was caused by work and obtained a medical certificate.
Notify the unit and fill out the occupational disaster notification form; the employer has legal reporting obligations.
When taking public sick leave: wages will be paid during treatment and recuperation.
Apply to the Labor Insurance Bureau for occupational accident insurance benefits (medical treatment, injury, illness, disability); the employer should assist.
If the employer does not provide assistance, you can appeal to the local labor bureau or call 1955.
no: Do not use ordinary sickness and illness leave to deal with occupational accidents (wage will be deducted).
Don't be asked to come back to work early when you're still feeling better.
entries.rep: Notification of workplace accidents; Labor Bureau/1955.
entries.ref: Workers’ Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Act; Workers’ Leave Rules, Article 6; Occupational Safety and Health Law, Article 37 (Employer’s Notification Obligation).
entries.ask: I was hit while riding my bicycle from Case A’s house to Case B’s house. Is this considered an occupational accident? Please tell me the documents to prepare and the application steps.

entries.s: When workers are in immediate danger (fire, gas, violence, unprotected from serious infectious diseases), they can stop their work and retreat to a safe place without being punished.
entries.why: You have the right to protect yourself first when danger occurs. The law clearly guarantees this, and the employer cannot punish you for this.
steps: Determine: Whether there is an immediate risk of danger on site (personal violence, fire, gas, structural danger, unprotected infectious diseases).
Retreat to a safe place and notify the supervisor immediately.
Record dangerous situations and retreat times.
Subsequently, the unit will evaluate whether to replace the waiter, improve the environment, or terminate the service.
Employers may not fire, transfer, withhold wages or take other adverse sanctions against workers who withdraw.
no: Don’t stick to a dangerous environment just for “service hours”.
Do not retreat without notifying your unit.
entries.rep: Supervision; in danger 110/119.
entries.ref: Article 18 of the Occupational Safety and Health Act (worker’s right to withdraw without adverse consequences from the employer).
entries.ask: The client’s son often loses his temper and throws things at home after drinking. Can I refuse to go? What should I tell my employer?

entries.s: The Labor Standards Act applies to residential workers: attendance must be recorded, 30-minute breaks should be given every 4 hours, overtime pay must be paid for overtime work, and transportation time is calculated according to the agreement.
entries.why: Fragmented shift schedules and long travel times between workers are the most common labor disputes among housekeepers.
steps: Confirm the labor contract: whether it is monthly salary, hourly salary or payment based on service hours, and how to calculate transportation time.
Attendance records must be true (check-in or APP) and do not make up after the fact.
Overtime pay or compensatory time off is required for working hours exceeding 8 hours per day or 40 hours per week.
Whether the moving time between clients is counted as working hours is subject to the interpretation of the Ministry of Contract and Labor. If you have any questions, you can ask the Labor Bureau.
The payslip must be understood clearly: basic salary, overtime pay, labor and health insurance, and retirement.
If there is a dispute, first communicate with the employer, and then appeal to the Labor Bureau or apply for mediation (free of charge).
no: Do not accept "verbal agreement" on wages and hours.
Do not sign a document voluntarily waiving overtime pay.
entries.rep: Unit Human Resources/Labor Bureau/1955.
entries.ref: Articles 30, 32, and 35 of the Labor Standards Act; Labor Accident Act (Labor Dispute Mediation).
entries.ask: I visit 5 clients a day and move for 2 hours in between. The unit only counts service hours. Is this reasonable? How can I confirm?

entries.t: Client absent at a scheduled visit
entries.s: Wait and try to contact, leave a record of the visit, and notify the supervisor; unmet time slots cannot be listed as services, and cannot be rewritten.
entries.why: The most common problem is not safety, but "recording": writing the period of no service as having service is an inaccurate publication. Another risk is to treat the encounter as a trivial matter and miss the signal that the client has actually collapsed in the house.
steps: After arriving on time, knock on the door, ring the bell, and call the client and family members 2-3 times each, and wait according to unit regulations (usually 15-30 minutes).

While waiting, observe whether there are any abnormalities: whether the lights are on, whether the shoes are there, whether there are any sounds or odors - if there are any abnormalities, please respond to "no one answers the door, lost contact" and directly call 110/119.

Nothing unusual: Take a photo of the door (no photos of the interior, no personal information other than the door number) as proof of visit, and leave a contact note in accordance with unit regulations.
Notify the supervisor by phone, and the supervisor will decide whether to wait, reschedule, or arrange for other cases.
The record of the day is written as "no visit": arrival and departure times, methods and results of contact attempts, supervision instructions; not listed as service hours.

If the patient is not encountered more than 2 times in a row, the supervisor and personal caretaker will understand the reasons (hospitalization, travel, family arrangements, wanting to terminate services) and adjust the plan.
no: Do not write the unmet period as already served, nor do you "do more to make up for it another day" but still publish the original date.
Don’t decide to “just come back next time” without reporting it.
Don’t extend the waiting time beyond the unit’s regulations without getting any reward.
entries.rep: Supervision; not encountered → supervisor in a row; abnormal → 110/119.
entries.ref: Application and payment methods for long-term care services (services must be actually provided before application can be made); unit visits did not meet the processing and transportation subsidy regulations; the business registration in Article 215 of the Criminal Law was untrue.
entries.ask: I went to the case’s home and waited for 20 minutes, but no one was there. The family said they were taking me to see a doctor temporarily. How should I write the correct service record this time?

entries.t: Traffic accidents during work or outings
entries.s: First confirm the safety of the person and call 110/119, do not move the car, do not reconcile privately, take photos and keep evidence, and report to the unit on the same day; accidents on the way to and from the case's home are occupational accidents.
entries.why: Residential service workers visit multiple homes a day. Traffic accidents are the most common occupational disaster, and they are also the most likely to give up their rights because of "fear of trouble."
steps: First confirm whether you and the client are injured; if someone is injured or if you are unsure, call 119. For any accident, call 110 and ask the police to come to the scene to record it (required for subsequent occupational accidents and insurance).
Do not move the vehicle (unless in a dangerous place), turn on double yellow lights and display triangle warning.
Take photos: panoramic view of the scene, vehicles and damage to both parties, license plates, road signs, and write down the other party’s name, phone number, car number, and insurance company.
Don’t talk about reconciliation or sign any documents on the spot, and don’t say “it’s my fault.”
Immediately notify the supervisor by phone; when accompanying the client out, notify family members and record the client's condition at the same time.
Seek medical treatment on the same day (even though I feel fine, the pain is much worse the next day), tell the doctor that I was injured while working, and get a diagnosis certificate.

Fill out an occupational accident report to your work unit, apply for the "Preliminary Analysis and Judgment Form of Road Traffic Accident" from the police, and apply for benefits under the labor occupational accident insurance; if you are riding your own car, also report it to your own insurance company.
no: Don’t think that an accident while riding your own motorcycle does not count as an occupational accident—traffic accidents that take a reasonable route between work and home will count.
Do not leave the scene to chase the next suspect.
Do not accept cash from the other party to settle the incident privately.
entries.rep: 110/119 → Supervision (notify family members when accompanying the client) → Notification of occupational accidents.
entries.ref: Labor Occupational Accident Insurance and Protection Law (Traffic Accidents During Commuting and Going Out for Business); Road Traffic Accident Handling Methods; Long-term Care Benefits and Payment Standards BA13 Accompanying outings, BA14 Accompanying medical treatment.
entries.ask: I was hit while riding my scooter from one client’s home to the next. The other party offers a private settlement of NT$5000. How should I assess this, and what documents should I prepare?

entries.t: Sales or solicitation by clients or families
entries.s: Always refuse, do not buy, do not join, do not keep personal information, do not introduce others; report to the supervisor for records and let the unit help set boundaries.
entries.why: Buying once is usually not just a one-time purchase; once there is money exchange, the service relationship becomes a human relationship, and it is more difficult to refuse later, and it is easy to cause disputes.
steps: Use "unit regulations" as the reason, be brief and firm: "Our unit stipulates that you cannot have business or money transactions with the client during your service period, please forgive me."
Do not fill in any information, do not join the LINE group, and do not receive samples or catalogs.
The other party continues to promote or pressures you with "If you don't buy, I won't let you serve" → Report to the supervisor on the same day and the unit will explain.

If the content of the promotion is suspected of fraud or the client himself has spent a large amount of money due to the promotion, observe and report it, and if necessary, report it based on negligence or property embezzlement.
Record what was pitched, when, and your response.
no: Don’t “buy once to show your support.”
Do not help make referrals to colleagues, other clients, or family members.
Do not assume it is acceptable to attend meetings or make donations simply because the solicitation is religious.
entries.rep: Supervision; the client is suspected of being defrauded or having property damaged → 165/113.
entries.ref: Unit Ethics and Regulations on Acceptance of Gifts; Multi-Level Marketing Management Law (reporting of illegal multi-level marketing); Article 43 of the Elderly Welfare Law (property misappropriation is within the scope of notification).
entries.ask: The client’s daughter is a direct seller. Every time she asks me to buy health food, she says that the client is also eating it. Please give me two ways to maintain the relationship and clearly refuse.

entries.t: Selling or promoting products to clients
entries.s: Using a service relationship to promote any products, direct sales, insurance, religion, or fundraising to clients violates the company's norms and professional ethics, and may lead to termination of the contract. Claiming curative effects or selling medicines may also violate the law.
entries.why: The client and his family trust you, and this trust makes it difficult for them to refuse; both law and ethics recognize this as "unjust enrichment taking advantage of a vulnerable position", and you have no protection in the event of an accident.
steps: Principle: During the service period and within a reasonable period after the case is closed, you shall not sell, recommend or purchase any goods, services or organizations in which you are interested in the case or your family members.

The client proactively asked "Do you have any recommended health food?": It only provides general health education information. It is recommended to consult a doctor, pharmacist or nutritionist, and no brands or purchasing agents are provided.
Health supplements and products must not claim to treat or prevent disease. Selling medicines requires the relevant pharmaceutical business authorization; home care workers must not do so.
If the promotion of insurance, investment, and religious donations causes losses to the client, it may involve civil compensation or even fraud and breach of trust.
The unit usually terminates the contract directly upon discovery and may notify the competent authorities.
If there is a product or side business that you want to promote, it should be completely separate from the client, not during service hours, and not with the client.
no: Don’t say “I am taking this myself and it is very effective” – this is a claim of efficacy.
Don’t use “I’ll help you buy it cheaper” to purchase products for which you get a commission.
Do not invite clients or family members to your direct sales, religious, or investment gatherings.
entries.rep: Unit ethics code; when reported, it will be handled by the competent authority and the unit.
entries.ref: Article 28 of the Food Safety and Hygiene Management Law (food shall not claim medical efficacy); Article 27 of the Pharmacy Law (selling of drugs requires a drug dealer license); Article 339 of the Criminal Law for fraud and Article 342 of breach of trust; unit service contract and code of ethics.
entries.ask: I usually make health food as a side job, and the client asked me if I could buy it. How can I respond so as not to violate the regulations?

entries.t: False service records and document falsification
entries.s: Any errors written in the records must be corrected and noted on the same day, and no corrections or additions should be made; writing down what was not done as done, and writing down a long time may constitute false business postings and fraud, and the money will be recovered and criminal liability will be imposed.
entries.why: Service records are proof that the government cancels long-term care benefits, and are not a trivial matter within the unit; "everyone writes like this" is not a legal reason.
steps: Correct approach: Record each service on the spot or on the same day, write the actual arrival and departure time, and the actual projects performed.

If errors are found (time, project, date): Do not blacken or use correction fluid, draw a line to retain the original words, write the correct content, signature and date next to it; the electronic system will correct the process according to the system and notify the supervisor.
Missing a note: make up the note as soon as possible and indicate the "make-up" and the actual date of the make-up. Do not write it down on the same day.
Periods that are not met, ended early, or refused by the client shall be recorded as they are and will not be recorded as service hours.

Being asked to "write more", "take longer", "help to make up for last week's writing": clearly refuse, keep a record of the conversation, and report it to the unit supervisor, the local health bureau or 1966; the identity of the whistleblower is protected.
When being checked: Explain truthfully, do not change records temporarily, and ask your employer to accompany you.
no: Don't write up a whole week's worth of records afterwards and write down today's date.
Do not check in outside the home and then go in in order to cooperate with the APP to check in.
Do not punch in or sign for colleagues.
Don’t just do something just because the supervisor says “it’ll be fine” – criminal liability is personal.
entries.rep: Record error → supervise correction; requested to post false information → refuse and report to the Health Bureau or 1966.
entries.ref: Article 215 of the Criminal Code for false business declarations (punishment of not more than 3 years), Article 210 for forgery of private documents, and Article 339 for obtaining money by fraud; the penalties below Article 47 of the Long-term Care Services Act (false declarations may be recovered and punished); unit records and write-off regulations.
entries.ask: I forgot to complete the record on the system yesterday, and I just thought of it today. Please tell me the correct way to make a record and what not to do.

entries.s: Adjust the texture and taste according to the client's teeth, swallowing and disease, and let the client participate in the steps that can be done; confirm kitchen safety (gas, knives, oil pans) first.
entries.why: Meal preparation is not about "cooking a meal for him," it is about letting him eat enough and eat safely while retaining what he can still do in the kitchen.
steps: Confirmation before service: What is approved is the client’s own meals and whether there are any restrictions at home (low salt, low sugar, limited water, soft, chopped, paste).
Ingredients handling: Separate raw and cooked food, and clean chopping boards and knives after use; for the elderly with poor immunity, overnight dishes should be heated thoroughly.

Texture: Change to soft texture (steamed, stewed) if the mouth is not good, and difficulty in swallowing. Chop, puree or add thickener according to speech therapy or nursing instructions; do not just serve porridge with pickles.

Each meal should have at least one portion of protein (eggs, tofu, fish, minced meat), one portion of vegetables, and one portion of staple food; the portion size should be estimated using the client’s fist.
Let the client participate in: washing vegetables, peeling garlic, setting out the dishes, and deciding on dishes. You can do it sitting down.
Before leaving: Turn off the gas, put out the fire, put away the knives, put the leftovers in the refrigerator with a date, and tell the client where the next meal will be.
no: Do not use ingredients from the client’s home to cook for family members or for yourself.
Do not leave the fire simmering while the client is alone.
Don’t supply only starch for a long time just because “he just wants to eat porridge”.
People with diabetes should not consume large amounts of thickening and sugary drinks.
entries.rep: The client has obviously been unable to eat, lost weight, and coughed repeatedly for more than a week → Notify the supervisor and recommend nutrition or swallowing evaluation.
entries.ref: Long-term care benefits and payment standards BA05 Meal care; the Minister of Health and Welfare’s Dietary Guidelines for the Elderly "My Plate".
entries.ask: The client lives alone, has diabetes, and only has one electric pot. Please help me design 5 dishes that can be completed in 20 minutes and can be divided into two meals.

entries.t: Shopping assistance and buying on behalf of clients
entries.s: First make a list and take the money, tell the price according to the order, hand in the invoice and change in person and record it; if you can go together, go together and let the client make his own choice.
entries.why: Shopping is the most likely item to cause money disputes, and it is also the most easily deprived of "autonomy" - many elderly people actually just need someone to accompany them, not someone to buy for them.
steps: Before going out, write a list with the client (or family members), confirm the budget, take cash and record the amount; you do not need to advance your own money.

Purchasing on behalf of the client is limited to daily necessities, subject to the approved scope; medicines are based on prescriptions, and tobacco and alcohol are usually not purchased on behalf of the client in accordance with unit regulations.
Keep invoices or receipts when making purchases, no less.
After coming back, order the goods, invoices, and change in person, and ask the client or family members to confirm and sign or mark on the record.
If the client is able to leave: change it to shopping with him, let him choose and pay by himself, and you are responsible for safety and lifting heavy objects.
Record: date, item, amount, change, confirmer.
no: Do not accept the client’s ATM card to collect money for purchasing.
Do not combine purchases for yourself or other clients with this client’s purchase at checkout.
Don't accept "no more change".
entries.rep: The amount does not match or is questioned → notify the supervisor immediately and provide invoices and records.
entries.ref: Long-term care benefits and payment standards BA16 Purchasing or collection or delivery services; Regulations on money transactions between units; Crime of embezzlement, Article 335 of the Criminal Law.
entries.ask: The client insists on not accepting change and tipping me every time he purchases on behalf of others. Please give me a polite way of saying no and the correct way to record it.

entries.s: Wear it while sitting, put on the affected side first and then take it off, straighten it without dragging it, pay attention to warmth and privacy; before every piece of clothing, ask "Which one do you want to wear?"
entries.why: Putting on and taking off clothes is an intimate contact twice a day. If done well, it is dignity, but if not done well, it will cause shoulder strain and skin tearing.
steps: Preparation: Close the windows, draw the curtains, fold the clothes in the order of wearing them, check the tightness, front and back, front and back first.
Posture: Able to sit (on the edge of the bed or a chair with armrests), and for bed sleepers, wear it in sections while lying on your side.

Top: Put the hand of the affected or weaker side first into the sleeve, pull it to the shoulder, and then put on the other side; when taking it off, do the opposite. The pullover is put on the arms first and then on the head.
Pants: When sitting, first put your feet into the trouser legs and pull them to your knees, stand up steadily (or roll over alternately) and then pull them to your waist.
Put on socks and shoes: Use a sock aid or roll up the socks before putting them on; choose heel covering or devil felt for shoes.
Elderly people with thin skin: When pulling up the sleeves, open the cuffs and put them over your hands. Do not grab the skin and push them in.
Leave it to the client to do what he can (unzipping, buttoning the center button).
no: Do not grab the wrist and pull the sleeve out (skin tear).
Do not take off all your clothes at once to save time.
Do not help the client decide what he will wear without asking.
entries.rep: If you find pain in the shoulder joint, skin tears, and obvious bruises when putting on and taking off → notify the supervisor.
entries.ref: Long-term care benefits and payment standards BA02 Basic daily care; Occupational therapy ADL assistance principles.
entries.ask: The patient’s joints in his hands are deformed, his fingers cannot be straightened, and it is difficult to wear a regular shirt. What are some clothing improvement and assistance techniques?

entries.s: Stand behind the weak side, put your hands behind your waist or belt, and let him control his balance; check the shoes, ground, and assistive devices before walking, and check his face and breathing while walking.
entries.why: "Walking with support" usually means walking by holding on to the arm. If the patient slips, you will reflexively pull up and fall together. The correct support is to protect the patient by the side, not to pull him.
steps: Before departure: shoes should be covered with non-slip materials, pants should not mop the floor, the ground should be dry, the route should be cleared, and assistive devices should be checked.
After standing up, stand still for 10–20 seconds and ask if you feel dizzy.
Your position: The patient's weak side, half a step behind; use one hand to gently support the back of the waist or grasp the displaced belt, and the other hand can be prepared in front.
Password: "Stand up first, then take a step." Let him go at his own speed. Don't pull or push.
When turning and threshold, stop first and then turn, take your time.
When you are about to fall: Don't hold on hard, protect your head and hips, and let him slide along your body to the ground or sit down.
After walking, sit down and rest, recording the distance and conditions.
no: Do not walk pulling on your arms or elbows.
Don’t walk and talk until you get distracted, or pick up things while walking.
Do not wait until the person is exhausted before turning back. Use only half of their available energy on the outward journey.
entries.rep: Walking suddenly becomes significantly unstable, dragging on one side, and breathing every time → Notify the supervisor and recommend referral for rehabilitation or medical treatment.
entries.ref: Long-term care benefits and payment standards BA02 basic daily care, BA13 accompanying outings; care attendant training: walking assistance.
entries.ask: The client has Parkinson's disease and suddenly freezes when walking. What commands or techniques can I use to help him get started?

entries.s: Meal delivery is a "nutritional catering service" and is performed by volunteers or personnel of the meal delivery unit. It is not a project for resident workers. When delivering meals, you must hand over the meals, confirm the patient's condition, and report any abnormalities immediately.
entries.why: Changzhao does have a meal delivery service, but it is a different benefit item from the home service. Resident service staff must know its rules before they can cooperate with the meal delivery unit and understand their role.
steps: Which one is it: "Nutritious catering services" for long-term care (home-based or community-based, payment code OT01), provided by meal delivery units commissioned by the county and city health bureaus, delivered to homes by meal delivery personnel or volunteers; the home service personnel correspond to BA05 meal care (meal preparation at home) and BA16 purchasing agency.

Who can use it: Those who have been assessed by the care center as being in need of long-term care and are eligible, and who are unable to go out to eat together; it is usually not applicable to those who have difficulty swallowing, can only be fed by tubes, or need special meals, nor are they employed by foreign caregivers (there are slight differences in each county and city).

What the meal delivery personnel should do: hand the meal to the client himself (leave without leaving it at the door), confirm that the client is at home and in normal condition, provide brief care, and fill in the meal delivery care record; if the client is unresponsive, falls, sick, or has an abnormal environment, immediately report the meal delivery unit and related units.

Meal boxes must be delivered within the specified time (mostly before 12:30 noon and 18:30 in the evening in various counties and cities) and must not be interrupted without reason; alternative methods can be used in case of natural disasters or Spring Festival.
Food safety: The lunch box should be kept hot or cold, and should not be detoured for too long; the client’s discomfort after meals should be recorded and reported.

The role of the resident attendant: If the client has meals delivered at the same time, he or she can assist in heating, packaging, observing whether the food has been eaten, putting the remaining food in the refrigerator to mark the date, and reporting the observed eating status to the supervisor.
no: Resident service staff should not promise "I will deliver food to you" on their own - it is not included in the approved items and there is no guarantee.
Food delivery personnel should not hang the food on the doorknob and leave without confirming the client.
Don’t just throw it away without repaying it just because the client hasn’t finished eating it for several days.
entries.rep: If the client does not answer the door or behaves abnormally during meal delivery → the meal delivery unit will report immediately and handle according to the lost contact and abnormal event process; the resident staff discovers that the meal delivery situation is abnormal → report to the supervisor, and a supervisor will contact the meal delivery unit.
entries.ref: Long-term care service application and payment method Nutritional catering service (OT01); Ministry of Health and Welfare’s nutritional catering service user qualification verification principles; Nutritional catering service demand instructions for each county and city (meal delivery care record, delivery time limit).
entries.ask: The client has long-term care to deliver meals, but every time I go there I see unfinished lunch boxes on the table. How should I observe, record and report back?

entries.s: Take it off and rinse it after each meal, brush it with a denture brush and water every day, take it off and soak it in water before going to bed; do not use toothpaste, soak it in hot water, or wear it all night.
entries.why: There is a film of bacteria and fungi on the surface of dentures. Wearing them overnight without cleaning them can cause oral mucositis and aspiration pneumonia; brushing them with toothpaste will scrape fine lines, making it easier for bacteria to adhere.
steps: Removal: Gently press the upper denture from behind to allow air to enter before taking it off. Gently rock the lower denture back and forth to take it out; operate on a sink filled with water to avoid breaking it.
Rinse: Rinse away food residues with clean water first.
Brush: Use a special brush for dentures or a soft-bristled toothbrush with water or denture cleaner to brush the inner, outer and fitting surfaces.
Soaking: Take it off before going to bed and soak it in water or denture cleaning tablet solution. Do not soak in hot water (it will deform).
The mouth itself should also be cleaned: the gums, palate, and tongue should be wiped with a soft toothbrush or gauze.
Before putting it back on, check whether there are any cracks, looseness, or worn mucous membranes; the dentures should be aligned correctly (up and down, left and right).
no: Do not use toothpaste on dentures.
Do not sleep with it on all night.
Do not soak in bleach or hot water.
Do not use adhesive to hold loose dentures in place; ask your dentist to adjust them.
entries.rep: Loose and worn dentures, white spots or ulcers on the oral mucosa for more than two weeks → Notify the supervisor and recommend dental treatment.
entries.ref: Ministry of Health and Welfare Oral Health Guidelines; Principles of Oral Care for the Elderly.
entries.ask: The client has dementia and will resist when the dentures are removed. What are the guidance methods to make him willing to cooperate?

entries.s: Use a small-headed toothbrush with soft bristles. The bristles should be pointed at an angle of 45 degrees to the gums. Brush two or two teeth back and forth in a short distance, 10 strokes per area, on both the inner and outer occlusal surfaces, and finally the tongue.
entries.why: The elderly have receding gums and exposed tooth roots. Brushing forcefully horizontally will damage the tooth roots. The Bethesda tooth brushing method is the most effective way to clean the gingival sulcus without damaging the teeth.
steps: Preparation: soft-bristle small-head toothbrush, bean-sized amount of fluoride toothpaste, water cup, basin or spittoon, towel.
Posture: Sitting or raising the head of the bed, tilt your head slightly forward, do not raise your head.
Angle: The bristles are angled at 45 degrees towards the gums, with the bristles half on the teeth and half on the gums.

Action: Two teeth at a time, brush back and forth 10 times in a short distance horizontally, and then move to the next area; the order is fixed (upper right and outer → upper left and outer → upper left and inner → upper right and inner, the same for the lower row).
Occlusal surface: brush back and forth; inner side of front teeth: brush upright and up and down.
Finally, brush the tongue 3-5 times from back to front, rinse your mouth or wipe it clean with gauze.
Hands are shaking or unable to hold: Wrap the handle of the toothbrush thickly (foam, towel) or use an electric toothbrush instead.
no: Do not use a hard-bristled or large-headed toothbrush.
Do not brush across a wide area with force.
Do not ask the client to lie down while brushing his or her teeth.
Replace the toothbrush after 3 months or when the bristles bloom.
entries.rep: Gums continue to bleed when brushing teeth, teeth shake, and bad breath is obvious → Notify the supervisor and recommend dentistry.
entries.ref: National Oral Health Guidelines of the Ministry of Health and Welfare (Belcher's Teeth Brushing Method).
entries.ask: The client has hemiplegia in his right hand and can only brush his teeth with his left hand. Please give me a handle improvement and brushing sequence that will allow him to brush his teeth by himself.

entries.s: Take 45 centimeters and wrap it around your middle finger, and control 1-2 centimeters with your thumb and index finger. Scrape it up and down against the tooth surface in a C shape, on both sides of each tooth gap; use a dental floss pick or interdental brush if the gap between teeth is large or your hands are not flexible.
entries.why: A toothbrush cannot clean the gaps between teeth. Plaque between teeth is the main cause of periodontal disease and tooth decay. The gaps between teeth become larger in the elderly and require more cleaning.
